Definition: to break forth as a bud, i.e. bloom; generally, to spread; specifically, to fly (as extending the wings); figuratively, to flourish
BiblicalUsage: Pârach is to break forth as a bud, to bloom, to spread. The vine in the cupbearer's dream has three branches, and it is as though it budded and her blossoms shot forth; the wilderness shall blossom as the rose; and God says I will be as the dew unto Israel, he shall grow as the lily, and cast forth his roots as Lebanon.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe blossoming is the Bible's picture of restoration. A desert blooms, a nation grows like a lily, and the dew does what no man's watering can.
